_doc: Forest set pieces, round 4 (ADR-0053): the trestle tunnel (w4_trestle_tunnel), an abandoned logging line's timber trestle over a dry ravine into a tunnel the Cordon blew. Models: tools/assetgen/blender/generators/props_wild4_trestle.py -> models/props/<id>[_worn|_destroyed].glb; catalog tools/assetgen/blender_catalogs/props_wild4_trestle.py; shared materials only. size = [width x, height y, depth z] in metres (Godot axes, front +Z) and is the collision box: the boxcar's is its floor block (vault in), the portal's and the hill's are the solid plinth under the tunnel's kit rooms.

defs.name: Trestle Bent
defs.description: One bent of a timber railway trestle: four creosoted posts (the outer two battered out) on a mudsill and concrete footings, a cap under the stringers, sway braces bolted across both faces and a girt half way up (worn: a brace hanging off, a post split).
defs._placement: Stand it on the ground under a trestle deck kit room at level 1 (its cap meets the deck section's stringers 0.6 m under the deck top); the bent's plane runs along x (rot 0 for a track along z).

defs.name: Trestle Deck Section
defs.description: 3.2 metres of trestle deck dressing: the stringers under the deck, the tie ends past its edges with a guard timber bolted along each side, and the two rails spiked on top (worn: a guard timber gone, rails rusted).
defs._placement: Place it on a trestle deck kit room (level 1, no y): origin on the deck's top at the track centre, the track along local z; the stringers hang 0.6 m under it.

defs.name: Track Section
defs.description: Three metres of logging-line track on a ballast bed: rough sawn ties and two light rails spiked to them, weeds and coal dust in the gravel (worn: a rail kinked, ties missing).

defs.name: Derailed Log Flatcar
defs.description: A logging flatcar off the rails at an angle, its front truck dropped into the ballast, three big logs chained on its bunks and a fourth rolled off beside it (worn: the deck boards split, a chain snapped).

defs.name: Boxcar
defs.description: A wooden-sided railway boxcar in oxide red on its trucks, the side door rolled open, its plank floor inside 1.15 m up (the collision box is the floor and underframe: vault in through the door). Lettered with the line's reporting marks (worn: boards sprung, rust bleeding from the bolts).
defs._placement: Origin at the car's centre on the rail head plane (y 0 on the tunnel floor); its door is on the +x side; put props inside it with y 1.15 (lumber stacks at the ends keep the walls honest).

defs.name: Lumber Bundle
defs.description: A bundle of green rough-sawn boards on two bearers, banded with strap iron and stencilled at the end (worn: a band burst, boards slid).

defs.name: Pump Handcar
defs.description: A section crew's pump handcar: a plank platform on four cast wheels, the walking beam on its A-frame with a handle each end, the brake lever and a tool box bolted on (worn: paint gone, a handle missing; destroyed: off one axle).

defs.name: Tunnel Collapse
defs.description: Where the far end came down: a slope of shattered rock, broken lagging and split timber sets packed to the crown of the bore, a twisted rail and the cab roof of a locomotive sticking out of it.

defs.name: Tunnel Portal
defs.description: The concrete face of a railway tunnel: piers, an arched ring and a headwall with the year cast in it, cracked and stained, a Cordon stencil sprayed across it (worn: spalled, the stencil faded). The bore behind it is the POI's own walls; only the face below the bore is solid.
defs._placement: Origin on the tunnel's outer wall face at the track centre, on the ground, facing out (+z): place it 0.09 m outside the wall line. The bore opening spans x -3.5..3.5 from 3.15 m to 8.95 m.

defs.name: Tunnel Hillside
defs.description: The rock and earth over a railway tunnel: a cut rock face either side and above the portal, a mossy brow with roots and a few boulders. The collision box is its plinth under the bore; above it the POI's own walls hold.
defs._placement: Origin at the plinth's centre on the ground; the tunnel's kit rooms stand on top of the plinth (their floor 3.15 m up).

defs.name: Timber Crib
defs.description: A crib of squared timbers laid log-cabin fashion and filled with rock: the trestle's abutment at the embankment (worn: timbers rotted, rock spilling).

defs.name: Key Board
defs.description: A painted board of cup hooks for padlock keys, each with a brass tag, the section foreman's stencilled list down the side (hang it ~1.2 m up).

defs.name: Spike Keg
defs.description: A nail keg of railway spikes with a claw bar leaning in it.

defs.name: Pile of Ties
defs.description: A crib-stacked pile of old railway ties, creosote black, weeds through them.
